name: Honey packet

card.summary: Single-serve honey sachets, usually with royal jelly, tongkat ali and ginseng, sold as natural vitality boosters whose energy and confidence claims people connect to looking and feeling their best.
card.aka: Royal Honey, Vital Honey, honey pack
card.note: The FDA has found undeclared sildenafil and tadalafil in many branded honey packets and warns of dangerous interactions with nitrates.

quick.overview:
Honey packets are small sachets of honey blended with ingredients such as royal jelly, bee pollen, tongkat ali and ginseng, marketed mainly for male libido, stamina and energy. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles they are discussed as an energy and vitality aid for training and nights out, and as a natural-sounding alternative to prescription supplements; the appearance link is indirect, through energy and confidence.

The US FDA has published notices for dozens of honey-based products after lab tests found sildenafil or tadalafil, the active drugs in Viagra and Cialis, that were not listed on labels. The agency says these can interact dangerously with nitrates.
quick.how: Packets are eaten straight from the sachet, usually in a single serving before an activity, and are sold online and in some stores. The listed ingredients are presented as natural. Plain honey is also used by lifters as a quick carbohydrate, which is a separate use.
quick.risks: Hidden sildenafil or tadalafil can lower blood pressure dangerously in people who take nitrates, such as those with diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol or heart disease. The FDA says it cannot test every product, and it advises talking to a health professional and reporting problems through MedWatch.

lead: Honey packets are single-serving sachets of a honey-based supplement sold chiefly for sexual performance and energy. Brands include Royal Honey VIP and Vital Honey, and labels typically list royal jelly, tongkat ali, bee pollen and ginseng [1].

Interest in them has spread through social media and college circles, with news coverage in 2024 describing alarm among health experts [1]. People who use them describe a pick-me-up for energy and confidence; the link to looks is indirect.

The FDA has issued warning letters to four companies and public notifications for 24 honey-based products, after lab analysis found undeclared sildenafil, tadalafil and in some cases acetaminophen [2].

Users report more energy and confidence
Feeling fit and energetic influences how they present themselves
angle.text: The appearance connection is indirect: marketing centres on energy, stamina and libido, and users describe feeling more confident and energetic. Packets are not marketed as a skin, hair or body-composition treatment.

paras: Honey packets resemble energy gels in a sachet. Marketing claims include improved sexual performance, delayed ejaculation and more energy and endurance, and Wikipedia notes that scientific support for the listed ingredients' effects is lacking [1].

The FDA warned in 2017 about undisclosed tadalafil in Royal Honey VIP, followed by a 2018 public notification; in April 2022 it advised against Royal Honey VIP after finding sildenafil, prompting a recall, and it issued a further notification in 2024 [1]. The FDA's current consumer page lists products including Black Thai Honey, Versace Real Honey for Men, HoneyGizer and Vital Honey, last updated April 22, 2026 [2].

Sildenafil and tadalafil are approved erectile dysfunction drugs meant for use under licensed supervision. In combination with nitrates they can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure [2]. The FDA points people to MedWatch and its problem-reporting form [2].

Honey packets come up in forums as one of several vitality or testosterone-adjacent products. Some users in training logs also describe plain honey packets as a fast carbohydrate source, which is a distinct everyday use.

No studies found on branded honey packets. Individual ingredients such as royal jelly and tongkat ali have limited clinical research, and the FDA's findings come from laboratory analysis of products [1][2].

timeline.event: FDA warns about tadalafil in Royal Honey VIP [1].
FDA advises against Royal Honey VIP after finding sildenafil; recall follows [1].
Further FDA notification on Royal Honey VIP [1].
